decisions.context: Fraud scores are needed before each transaction is authorized, so predictions must be computed in the request path. Precomputing scores would risk using stale results.

alternatives.label: Queue-fronted online serving cluster
pros: Low latency: distributes online predictors
Peak availability: queue supports load balancing
cons: Low latency: queue adds a request hop
Peak availability: cluster needs capacity management

alternatives.label: Precomputed offline serving
pros: Peak availability: results are ready to read
Cost: scores can be computed in batches
cons: Low latency: misses current transaction context
Peak availability: stale results may be unusable

decisions.rationale: Latency decides the choice: scoring must use the current transaction, so online serving is required. This gives up the lower request-path cost of batch computation and adds queue operations.
consequences: Keep serving replicas available for peak traffic.
Operate the queue and serving cluster as critical-path components.

decisions.context: The scorer needs fast feature reads, while auditors need a durable record of the features used. One storage path may not serve both access patterns well.

alternatives.label: Online/offline feature-store architecture
pros: Low latency: online store serves inference features
Audit traceability: offline store preserves feature data
cons: Low latency: feature synchronization adds work
Audit traceability: storage lineage must be maintained

alternatives.label: Central analytical ML data platform
pros: Audit traceability: shared platform exposes prepared data
Cost: consolidates analytical data workflows
cons: Low latency: analytical reads may be too slow
Audit traceability: inference-time feature snapshot is not explicit

decisions.rationale: Latency decides the choice: online features serve the scoring request, with durable offline data supporting traceability. The cost is keeping the online and offline representations consistent.
consequences: Record feature versions or snapshots for each score.
Maintain synchronization between online and durable feature stores.

decisions.context: Auditors must be able to determine which model version and features produced a score. Tracking only the model artifact would leave the input data lineage incomplete.

alternatives.label: Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability
pros: Audit traceability: links runs, datasets, artifacts, and metadata
Reproducibility: captures training and pipeline context
cons: Cost: requires integrated metadata governance
Reproducibility: records must be retained and queryable

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
pros: Audit traceability: identifies deployed model artifacts
Cost: narrower tracking scope
cons: Audit traceability: does not link each score to its features
Reproducibility: omits dataset and run context

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides the choice: it connects model artifacts with training runs and datasets, which artifact-only tracking does not. The trade-off is the added work of capturing and retaining lifecycle metadata.
consequences: Attach model and feature identifiers to each score record.
Retain lineage metadata for the audit period.

decisions.context: The transaction authorization path needs a real-time prediction interface that the payments application can call. A model bundled into the application would couple its release cycle to the application’s.

alternatives.label: Model-as-a-service deployment
pros: Low latency: exposes a direct real-time prediction service
Peak availability: serving can scale independently
cons: Low latency: adds a network call
Peak availability: introduces a service dependency

alternatives.label: Model-as-dependency deployment
pros: Low latency: avoids a service network hop
Peak availability: model ships with the application
cons: Peak availability: application capacity also carries scoring load
Audit traceability: model updates follow application releases

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: independent serving capacity can scale with scoring demand. The system gives up the lower latency and simpler operation of an in-process model call, so the service hop must fit the latency budget.
consequences: Keep model serving independently deployable and scalable.
Include service-call overhead in the scoring latency budget.

decisions.context: The service must continue operating during peaks, and its scores and inputs may need investigation later. Monitoring only model quality would miss latency, uptime, and data-quality failures.

alternatives.label: Service-health and data-quality monitoring
pros: Peak availability: tracks latency, uptime, and dependencies
Audit traceability: observes data quality and shifts
cons: Peak availability: monitoring adds operational overhead
Audit traceability: metrics alone do not preserve score-level evidence

alternatives.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
pros: Peak availability: surfaces generic service issues
Cost: avoids ML-specific monitoring setup
cons: Audit traceability: misses feature and data changes
Peak availability: cannot explain model behavior

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: service health and dependency signals expose production failures, while data-quality monitoring helps investigate scoring inputs. The trade-off is added monitoring effort, and score-level audit records still need explicit lineage capture.
consequences: Alert on latency, uptime, dependencies, and data-quality failures.
Link monitoring events to score and lineage records where possible.
